title: stabilize tokenizer-template alignment and publish-safe checks for onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Several recent model onboarding runs surfaced subtle misalignment between the tokenizer's subtoken boundaries and the chat template serializers used by the runtime. Mismatches lead to small but user-visible prompt truncation, role delimiter duplication, and incorrect prefix KV caching leading to unexpected latency/cost regressions when a new model is published and pinned.

Goal: Implement a conservative, automated safety net that detects tokenizer↔template incompatibility during onboarding, prevents publishing incompatible performance profiles, and provides deterministic fallback behavior (two-phase pinning + canary runtime rollout). The feature should be lightweight to avoid blocking onboarding for models that are clearly compatible and must produce actionable diagnostics for oncall/SEs.

Scope: 1) runtime-side "template-sentinel" header that the onboarding harness can use to validate role delimiter and tokenization invariants; 2) an offline fuzzy-token alignment scorer that compares model tokenizer outputs against canonical chat templates and flags regressions above thresholds; 3) publish gating: block performance-profile publishing for models failing critical checks and surface remediation steps in the onboarding UI; 4) automated canary pin rollout that pins a model only in a subset of traffic if non-critical mismatches exist.

Tradeoffs considered: - Strict gating prevents bad profiles from reaching customers but increases time-to-publish; use tiered gating (hard vs soft checks) to balance. - Runtime instrumentation adds marginal latency; we limit sentinel checks to onboarding path and sampling in production canaries. - Fuzzy alignment must avoid false positives on legitimate tokenizer differences (e.g., new vocab) by weighting semantic delimiter errors higher than whitespace tokenization drift.

Deliverables: - tokenizer-template sentinel header and runtime validation hooks (PR #3241) - fuzzy alignment scorer library + onboarding integration - onboarding UI warnings and publish-block with remediation links - QA checklist and automated regression tests - telemetry events for mismatch types and severity
comments: 2026-02-15 — Spike complete: validated sentinel header approach against 8 internal models; found delimiter duplication with two open-source models. Results documented in Confluence.

2026-02-20 — Design review with PM/Design: agreed on hard vs soft check categories and user-facing message copy. Decided to block profile publishing for hard checks only; soft checks will create warnings and require explicit override with justification.

2026-02-25 — Engineering: landed initial fuzzy alignment scorer prototype (benchmarked on 50 templates). Scoring thresholds tuned to 0.08 for hard failures based on SNR analysis. See benchmark table in PR notes.

2026-03-02 — QA: integration test harness added to CI to run validator against model bundle artifacts; discovered edge-case for unicode delimiter in Japanese chat templates and added normalization step.
2026-03-07 — PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3241 (tokenizer-sentinel + onboarding hooks). Requesting review from @sofiar and @danielk.

2026-03-10 — Canaries: smoke canary run started against staging for runtime-1.22 with two-phase pin rollout; observed no perf regressions but two soft warnings for model-cc-2025. Filed follow-up ENG-99310 for remediation guidance generation.
qa_checklist: Unit tests for fuzzy alignment scorer covering delimiter, whitespace, and multibyte cases
Integration test: onboarding harness validates sentinel header for at least 12 canonical templates
End-to-end test: publish gating rejects hard failures and allows override with audit log
Canary rollout: two-phase pin executed with 5% -> 50% traffic increase steps and rollback script
Performance: confirm <2% median token-latency impact when sentinel enabled in onboarding path
Telemetry: mismatch_event emitted with type, severity, example input, and model_version
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding harness runs validator automatically and classifies mismatches as hard or soft based on scorer thresholds
Performance-profile publish is blocked for hard failures and the UI surfaces clear remediation steps and links to diagnostic logs
Two-phase pin rollout implemented: initial pin can be restricted to canary routes and automatically rolled back on perf or quality regressions
All new checks have CI coverage and are included in pre-merge pipelines
Telemetry shows mismatch types and rates; SLO for false positive rate <3% over a 48h rolling window during canary
